claim: mobjinfo[NUMMOBJTYPES] OOB read flagged after the doomednum-match loop (p_mobj.c:623,767)
rationale: Both sites are guarded by 'if (i==NUMMOBJTYPES) I_Error(...)' immediately before the mobjinfo[i] access; I_Error ends in exit(-1) (noreturn). cppcheck does not model the C11 _Noreturn keyword on the i_system.h prototype, so it assumes I_Error returns and reports a phantom OOB. Code is correct.

claim: player->ammo[NUMAMMO]/ammo[-1] OOB flagged in P_GiveAmmo (p_inter.c:87)
rationale: Guarded by 'if (ammo < 0
topic: | ammo >= NUMAMMO) I_Error(...)' (DOOM-0021 fixed the >NUMAMMO off-by-one to >=). I_Error is noreturn (exit -1) but cppcheck does not model C11 _Noreturn, so it cannot see the guard short-circuits the access. cppcheck's own 'condition redundant OR index accessed' wording confirms the guard. Code is correct.|cppcheck-noreturn-not-modeled

claim: s_sound.c:665 uninitvar 'music' in S_ChangeMusic
rationale: music is set in the if/else at 657-663: the bad-number branch calls I_Error (exit -1, _Noreturn), the else assigns &S_music[musicnum]. So music is always initialised at line 665. cppcheck does not model C11 _Noreturn, so it cannot see the I_Error branch never falls through. Same blind spot as p_mobj/p_inter. Code is correct.

claim: i_sound.c:346 negativeIndex vol_lookup[leftvol*256] in I_SetChannels/updateSoundParams
rationale: leftvol is clamped at 341-342: 'if (leftvol < 0 || leftvol > 127) I_Error(...)'. I_Error is _Noreturn, so leftvol is in [0,127] at line 346 and vol_lookup[leftvol*256] is in range. cppcheck cannot model the noreturn guard. Code is correct.

claim: p_enemy.c:381-382 nullPointer actor->target in P_NewChaseDir
rationale: actor->target is null-checked at 375-376: 'if (!actor->target) I_Error(...)'. I_Error is _Noreturn, so actor->target is non-null when dereferenced at 381-382. cppcheck cannot model the noreturn guard. Code is correct.

claim: p_mobj.c:306 shiftNegativeLHS 'mo->player->deltaviewheight = mo->momz>>3'
rationale: momz is fixed_t (signed). The arithmetic right shift of a negative value is the intended fixed-point divide-toward-negative-infinity for the landing squat. On every platform DOOM targets (two's complement, gcc) >> on a negative int is an arithmetic shift. Replacing with /8 would change rounding (toward zero) and alter the squat feel. Intentional original DOOM behaviour - do not touch.

claim: p_pspr.c:530 integerOverflow '-0x40000000/20' (ANG90) in A_Saw turn-to-face
rationale: ANG90 is 0x40000000 (angle_t). The expression 'angle - player->mo->angle' is deliberate unsigned angle_t wrap arithmetic compared against signed -ANG90/20; the values do not actually overflow at runtime (-0x40000000/20 = -53687091, well within int). This is load-bearing original DOOM angle math used identically in every port. Touching it would break the chainsaw turn-to-face. Intentional - do not touch.

claim: r_things.c:438 negativeIndex patch->columnofs[texturecolumn] in R_DrawVisSprite
rationale: The range check at 433-436 is under '#ifdef RANGECHECK'. In release builds texturecolumn is kept in range by the upstream vis->x1/x2 clamping in R_ProjectSprite, exactly as in vanilla DOOM and Chocolate Doom. Adding an unconditional clamp here would change renderer behaviour (skip columns vanilla would draw). Project goal is to keep original DOOM rendering. Leave as-is.

claim: am_map.c:411 integerOverflow 'max_x - min_x' in AM_findMinMaxBoundaries
rationale: min_x/max_x are seeded with MAXINT/-MAXINT then narrowed to real vertex coordinates by the loop at 398-409. A loaded map always has vertices, and map coords are bounded far below MAXINT, so the subtraction never underflows in practice. cppcheck assumes the worst-case seed range. Theoretical only; vanilla code. Leave as-is.

claim: p_switch.c:123 arrayIndexOutOfBounds alphSwitchList[41] accessed at index 49 in P_InitSwitchList
rationale: The loop `for (i=0; i<MAXSWITCHES; i++)` (MAXSWITCHES=50, p_spec.h:241) reads alphSwitchList[i].episode and `break`s on the terminator entry {"\0","\0",0} (episode==0) which sits at index 41 in the 42-entry literal. So i never exceeds 41 at runtime; index 49 is cppcheck's worst-case loop-bound assumption ignoring the in-bounds terminator. Vanilla DOOM; safe as long as the terminator stays within MAXSWITCHES, which it does.

claim: f_finale.c:626 arrayIndexOutOfBoundsCond patch->columnofs[8] accessed at index 319 in F_DrawPatchCol
rationale: columnofs is a flexible-array-member declared `int columnofs[8]` in patch_t (r_defs.h) as a placeholder; the real length equals the patch's width. F_BunnyScroll draws the 320-wide END/bunny patches, so columnofs has 320 real entries and index 319 is in range. cppcheck assumes the declared placeholder size 8. Same flexible-array class as r_things.c columnofs. Vanilla; safe.

claim: d_main.c:613 nullPointerRedundantCheck home in IdentifyVersion (sprintf basedefault from $HOME)
rationale: `home = getenv("HOME"); if (!home) I_Error(...)` guards the subsequent use. I_Error is _Noreturn (i_system.h, DOOM-0023), so home is non-null at the sprintf. cppcheck does not model C11 _Noreturn so it treats the !home branch as fall-through. Same noreturn blind spot as the p_mobj/p_inter/s_sound ledger entries. Code is correct.

claim: i_net.c:237 & i_net.c:318 nullPointerRedundantCheck '!hostentry' (gethostbyname result deref)
rationale: Both sites are `hostentry = gethostbyname(...); if (!hostentry) I_Error(...); ...hostentry->h_addr_list...`. I_Error is _Noreturn (i_system.h, DOOM-0023), so hostentry is non-null at the deref. cppcheck does not model C11 _Noreturn — same blind spot as the p_mobj/p_inter/s_sound/d_main ledger entries. Code is correct.

claim: p_doors.c:223 identicalConditionAfterEarlyExit '!p' second condition always false in EV_DoLockedDoor
rationale: EV_DoLockedDoor early-exits with `p = thing->player; if (!p) return 0;` before the switch, so the per-case `if (!p) return 0;` guards are redundant (always false). This is verbatim vanilla linuxdoom-1.10 code — id left the per-case checks in. Harmless dead redundancy, not a bug; project keeps original DOOM behaviour. Leave as-is.

claim: g_game.c:1466 redundantAssignment 'viewactive' reassigned before use in G_InitNew
rationale: G_InitNew sets `viewactive = true;` at ~1461 then again at ~1466. The duplicate is verbatim vanilla linuxdoom-1.10 (id's original G_InitNew). Behaviour-neutral; assigning true twice has no effect. Not a bug; deleting it is an orthogonal edit to vanilla code (rule 11). Leave as-is.

claim: f_wipe.c:110 knownConditionTrueFalse 'else if (*w < *e)' always true in wipe ColorXForm
rationale: Inside `if (*w != *e) { if (*w > *e) {...} else if (*w < *e) {...} }` the trailing `*w < *e` is provably always true (the two values differ and the >-branch was taken otherwise). cppcheck is technically right, but it's vanilla linuxdoom-1.10 defensive code equivalent to a plain `else`. Behaviour-correct; not a bug. Leave as-is.

claim: semgrep/grep flag ~90 strcpy/sprintf/strcat 'unsafe C function' uses across the engine (d_main.c, g_game.c, m_menu.c, hu_stuff.c, wi_stuff.c, i_sound.c, sndserv, etc.).
rationale: These are regex matches on the function name, not exploitable flows. The DOOM sources copy compile-time string literals (e.g. strcpy(savedescription,\"NET GAME\"), strcpy(name,\"INTERPIC\")) or bounded data (sprintf(name,\"map0%i\",map) with map a small int) into adequately-sized fixed buffers. No attacker-controlled data crosses a trust boundary in a local single-player engine. Per the audit's own PHASE 2, confirm exploitability not keyword match. Reassess only if a specific call takes unbounded external input into an undersized buffer.

claim: [CRITICAL] Command injection: i_sound.c:791 sndserver = popen(buffer, "w").
rationale: buffer is built from sndserver_filename (compile-time default "./sndserver ", overridable only via the user's own default.cfg "sndserver" var) plus the user's own $DOOMWADDIR env, then "-quiet". This is how DOOM launches its own sound-server child process by design; all inputs are local and self-controlled in a single-player engine. No untrusted/remote data reaches the command. Not attacker-reachable. (The whole legacy sndserver path is also superseded by SDL2 audio, DOOM-0004.)

claim: cppcheck: Array 'mobjinfo[137]' accessed at index 137 (out of bounds) at p_mobj.c:623 (P_RespawnSpecials) and p_mobj.c:767 (P_SpawnMapThing).
rationale: Same class as the existing p_inter.c noreturn entry. Each access is immediately preceded by 'for(i=0;i<NUMMOBJTYPES;i++) ...; if(i==NUMMOBJTYPES) I_Error(...)'. I_Error is _Noreturn (DOOM-0023) so i<NUMMOBJTYPES is guaranteed at the mobjinfo[i] access, but cppcheck does not model I_Error as noreturn and so treats i==137 as reachable. The DOOM-0020 guard is present and correct. Code is correct.

claim: ~90 MAJOR strcpy/strcat/sprintf "unsafe C function" + semgrep findings across linuxdoom-1.10 (d_main.c, g_game.c, m_menu.c, m_misc.c, hu_stuff.c, i_sound.c, d_net.c, sndserv/) indicate buffer-overflow risk.
rationale: False positives: all are faithful 1997 id Software calls copying STRING LITERALS (e.g. DEVDATA"default.cfg", "NET GAME", EMPTYSTRING, "ds%s"+8-char WAD lump names) or bounded inputs into buffers sized to hold them; no attacker-influenced unbounded source reaches them. Verified by data-flow tracing. The project preserves id's code verbatim and only fixes genuinely-reachable overflows. The ONE real exception (G_RecordDemo, g_game.c:1553, unbounded -record CLI arg into demoname[32]) was fixed under DOOM-0070. Do not re-flag the literal/bounded calls.

claim: [CRITICAL] Command Injection — i_sound.c:794 sndserver = popen(buffer, "w").
rationale: False positive: the popen call lives in the legacy SNDSERV external-sound-server block which is NOT compiled in the modern build (no -DSNDSERV in the Makefile; audio is SDL2_mixer). The block is dead code; `buffer` is built from a fixed internal sndserver path, not attacker input, even if it were compiled. Unreachable -> not exploitable.

claim: [MINOR] CMake find_package without version floor (mingw-deps/Vulkan-Headers/.../CMakeLists.txt:13) and 14 [MINOR] Debug/Temp-Code findings.
rationale: False positives / out of scope: all live under mingw-deps/ (vendored upstream Vulkan-Headers + SDL2 dev libs, regenerable per mingw-deps/README.md, gitignored) — not project source. The one in-tree debug match (hu_stuff.c:813) is already a commented-out 1997 debug line, harmless. Exclude vendored trees from project audits.

claim: [MAJOR] Continuous Integration Missing — no .github/workflows etc.
rationale: Not a correctness/security defect — an infrastructure choice. The project ships via a hand-run AppImage packaging script and manual GitHub Releases; CI is a possible future enhancement, not an audit fix target. Noted, not actioned.

claim: cppcheck portability: intToPointerCast (p_mobj.c:425,434; p_tick.c:83,108), shiftNegativeLHS (p_mobj.c:306), CastAddressToIntegerAtReturn (d_net.c:93).
rationale:
All vanilla 1997 id code. The int<->pointer casts are DOOM's thinker-function sentinel idiom (function.acp1/acv casts) and packet-address returns; shiftNegativeLHS is vanilla fixed-point math. Correct on the LP64 x86-64 Linux target the project builds for; cppcheck's 'portability' class flags theoretical non-portability, not a defect. Preserve-vanilla; not actionable.</rationale>

claim: cppcheck error: Signed integer overflow for expression '-0x40000000/20' at p_pspr.c:530.
rationale:
Vanilla autoaim turn-to-face code: `-ANG90/20` where ANG90==0x40000000 (angle_t). DOOM angle arithmetic is unsigned 32-bit and relies on wraparound; -0x40000000/20 = -53687091 does not actually overflow int. cppcheck mis-evaluates the constant sub-expression. Verbatim id code; intended DOOM autoaim behaviour. Not a defect.</rationale>

claim: cppcheck error: syntax error at r_vulkan.cpp:6335 [syntaxError].
rationale:
cppcheck cannot fully parse the C++23 Vulkan backend; the file compiles cleanly with g++ -std=c++23 and links into linuxxdoom. A cppcheck C++-frontend limitation, not a code defect -- and it means cppcheck gives no real coverage of r_vulkan.cpp (the indie-review lanes cover it instead). Not actionable.</rationale>

claim: cppcheck style: duplicateAssignExpression ry/nx (r_mesh.c:1083) and shadowVariable 'menuactive' (i_video.c:232,403).
rationale:
r_mesh: ry=-cosf(a) and nx=-cosf(a) are BOTH correctly -cos(a) per the documented camera screen-right (sin a,-cos a) and billboard-normal (-cos a,-sin a) vectors -- a coincidental shared value, not a copy-paste bug. i_video: the two `extern boolean menuactive;` are function-scope extern declarations pulling in the m_menu.c global (idiom to avoid a header include), not locals shadowing it. Both are cppcheck misreading intentional code. Not defects.</rationale>

claim: commits.md:46 "push after each logical batch" conflicts with global CLAUDE.md rule 6's "push after each release" (flagged CRITICAL push-cadence conflict).
rationale: Not a conflict. Global CLAUDE.md rule 6 gives PUBLIC repos unlimited free CI minutes and says push freely; the "after each release" cadence is the PRIVATE-repo rule. DOOM_Ants is a public repo (gh visibility PUBLIC; commits.md:46 states "This is a public repo"), so "push after each logical batch" is fully consistent with the global rule. The cold reviewer applied the private-repo clause to a public repo.

claim: dependencies.md:166-170 ("Bump and idiom-refresh ship together") is a near-duplicate of global CLAUDE.md rule 5b and should be reduced to a one-line reference.
rationale: Not project-internal duplication. The "other doc" is the user's PRIVATE global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, which is not in the DOOM_Ants repo and is not shipped to contributors. A contributor who clones the repo needs this rule stated in dependencies.md; replacing it with a reference to a machine-local file they do not have would break the standard. Cold-eyes dedup applies to intra-project duplication only.

claim: renderer.md misc5 push-constant row lists z/w as reserved but they are in use (de-tile quality / dirt-colour / filth toggle); table needs updating.
rationale: Stale-roadmap echo. The reviewer read ROADMAP bullet DOOM-0194 ("Fix the stale misc5 push-constant comment in pathtrace.comp"), which is already ✅ shipped (ROADMAP.md:1807). Verified directly: renderer.md's misc5 table row already lists all four components (x=grime id, y=de-tile quality, z=dirt-colour id, w=filth toggle) and pathtrace.comp's misc5 struct comment (lines ~259-264) matches. Nothing says "reserved". No current defect.
